# UTF-8 truncation keeps a complete character that ends at the byte limit

The original replacement returns the previous boundary only when the advanced distance exceeds maxBytes or decoding reports an error. A complete character at the exact byte limit remains included, and invalid input preserves the valid prefix scanned so far. The infallible output-parameter API becomes an owning nsCString return assigned by its production receiver. The sixteen literal tests assert boundary and invalid-prefix examples. Accepted source later changes the algorithm and size type; no fresh GTest or production operation ran.

Scope: MailNews UTF-8 string truncation.
